toc.title: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications (skills 3.3.2 and 3.3.3)

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EMR: Elastic MapReduce; SNS: Simple Notification Service; YARN: Yet Another Resource Negotiator; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; SDK: software development kit; SMS: Short Message Service; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; DLQ: dead-letter queue; ELB: Elastic Load Balancing; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; URI: Uniform Resource Identifier; HDFS: Hadoop Distributed File System; WLM: workload management; RDS: Relational Database Service

  • Deploy logging and monitoring so pipelines are auditable and traceable
  • Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics, alarms and notifications to send alerts
  • Troubleshoot performance and maintain AWS Glue and Amazon EMR pipelines
  • Use AWS CloudTrail to track API calls
  • Use CloudWatch Logs to log application data, with a focus on configuration and automation
  • Analyze logs with Athena, EMR, OpenSearch Service and CloudWatch Logs Insights
  • Extract logs for audits

2What to Monitor and Why

Running case

Kestrel Freight Watches the Pipeline

  • The pipeline finished two hours late last Tuesday and nobody knew until a customer called
  • Glue job runtime doubled after a source change
  • A new engineer deleted a table: who did it?
  • Your job: see problems early, alert the right people, and find the cause fast
Signal Tool Answers
Metrics (numbers over time) Amazon CloudWatch Is it healthy and fast? (runtime, errors, lag, throughput, capacity)
Logs (event text) CloudWatch Logs What happened in this run?
API activity AWS CloudTrail Who did what, when, from where (changes and access)?
Events Amazon EventBridge State changes (job failed, crawler finished) to react
Alerts CloudWatch alarms → Amazon SNS Tell people or systems
Exam tip

Metrics, logs and CloudTrail answer different questions: performance (CloudWatch metrics), what the code said (CloudWatch Logs), who changed something (CloudTrail).

3CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications (skills 3.3.2 and 3.3.3)

  • Metrics: services publish them automatically (Glue job metrics, Kinesis IteratorAgeMilliseconds and throughput, Lambda errors and throttles and duration, Step Functions failed executions, DynamoDB throttled requests, Redshift CPU and queue length, EMR cluster and YARN metrics, MWAA scheduler and worker health); you can publish custom metrics (record counts, data freshness) with the SDK or the embedded metric format
  • Alarm: watches one metric (or a math expression) and is in OK, ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA; set the threshold, period and number of data points; composite alarms combine alarms to reduce noise; anomaly detection learns a normal band
  • Alarm actions: notify an SNS topic (email, SMS, chat, ticket, Lambda), start an automatic fix (Lambda, Systems Manager, Auto Scaling), or stop or recover an EC2 instance
  • Dashboards show metrics together; Managed Grafana is the alternative
  • EventBridge rules catch state-change events (Glue job FAILED or TIMEOUT, crawler failed, EMR step failed) and route them to SNS or Lambda
  • Useful pipeline alarms: job failed or ran longer than normal, stream iterator age rising (consumers lagging), Lambda errors or throttles, DLQ depth above zero, data freshness (no new data in N hours), zero rows written
  • Delay notification threshold on a Glue job warns when a run takes longer than expected
Exam tip

"Alert the team when a Glue job fails" → EventBridge rule on the Glue job state change (or a CloudWatch alarm) to an SNS topic. "Know that Kinesis consumers are falling behind" → alarm on GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds.

4CloudWatch Logs (skills 3.3.7 and 3.3.8)

  • CloudWatch Logs stores log events in log groups (an application or job) and log streams (a source, such as one run); services send logs there: Lambda, Glue (including continuous logging so logs appear during the run), ECS (the awslogs driver), API Gateway, MWAA, Step Functions (Express), EC2 (via the CloudWatch agent)
  • Configuration and automation focus:
    • Set retention per log group (the default is never expire) to control cost
    • Create log groups and permissions with infrastructure as code
    • Metric filters turn patterns in logs into metrics (count ERROR lines), which feed alarms
    • Subscription filters stream log events in near real time to Kinesis Data Streams, Data Firehose or Lambda (and from there to S3 or OpenSearch); cross-account delivery is supported
    • Export to S3 for archives and Athena
    • Use structured JSON logs with run ID, step and record counts, and log levels
    • Log classes (Standard and Infrequent Access) trade features for lower cost [Verify live]
  • CloudWatch Logs Insights: a query language to search and analyze log groups interactively: fields, filter, stats, sort, limit, parse
fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /ERROR/
| stats count() as errors by bin(5m)
| sort errors desc
Analyze logs with Best for
CloudWatch Logs Insights Quick interactive queries on recent logs in CloudWatch
Amazon Athena SQL over logs in S3 (CloudTrail, ELB, VPC flow, application logs) at low cost; use partitioning or partition projection
Amazon OpenSearch Service Search, dashboards and real-time log analytics (ingest through Firehose or subscription filters)
Amazon EMR (Spark) Very large volumes and custom processing of big data application logs
Glue / Spark Batch parsing and enrichment of raw logs into Parquet
Exam tip

"Run SQL on years of logs in S3 cheaply" → Athena (partitioned). "Near-real-time search and dashboards over logs" → OpenSearch Service fed by Firehose. "Count ERROR lines and alarm" → metric filter + alarm.

5Troubleshooting and Maintaining Pipelines (skills 3.3.4 and 3.3.6)

AWS Glue

  • Turn on: job metrics, observability metrics, continuous logging and the Spark UI (event logs in S3)
  • Read: CloudWatch driver and executor memory, executors running, bytes read and written; job run insights for root causes; the Spark UI for skew, shuffle and stage time
  • Typical fixes: bigger or memory-optimized workers, more workers (or auto scaling), fix skew, group small files, push down filters, enable bookmarks, raise timeouts only for a reason
  • Maintain: update scripts and libraries, move to current Glue versions, rotate secrets, review failed runs, keep job parameters in code, and review the pipeline against the Well-Architected pillars with the AWS Well-Architected Tool

Amazon EMR

  • Logs: step logs, container logs (YARN) and node logs; EMR archives logs to S3 at a set interval (turn on log URI so logs survive cluster termination)
  • Monitor: CloudWatch metrics (applications running, YARN memory available, HDFS utilization, core and task node health), the Spark History Server and YARN ResourceManager UI
  • Fix: resize or add task nodes, managed scaling, tune executors and memory, replace unhealthy nodes, use Spot with fallback for task nodes

Performance issues in general

Symptom Check Fix
Pipeline slower than usual Input volume or file count changed, skew, throttling Scale out, repartition, compact files, raise capacity
Stream lag Iterator age, consumer errors, shard limits More shards, enhanced fan-out, parallelization factor
Lambda slow or failing Duration, errors, throttles, memory More memory, reserved concurrency, batch size
Redshift queries slow Queue wait, table design, WLM Sort and distribution keys, concurrency scaling, materialized views
Exam tip

"After a source change, a Glue job is much slower" → check job metrics and the Spark UI for skew or many small files, then fix partitioning and file layout.

6AWS CloudTrail (skill 3.3.5)

  • CloudTrail records API calls and account activity: who (identity), what (action, resource), when, from where (IP, console, SDK), and result
  • Event types: management events (control plane: create, delete, change), data events (data plane: S3 object reads and writes, Lambda invokes, DynamoDB item access; off by default, extra cost), Insights events (unusual API activity)
  • Event history: the console keeps the last 90 days of management events at no charge [Verify live]; for longer retention and all event types create a trail that delivers to S3 (and optionally CloudWatch Logs)
  • Use it for: who deleted the table, security investigations, compliance, detecting unusual changes; query with Athena or CloudTrail Lake (Module 17)
  • Integrity: log file validation shows files were not altered
Exam tip

"Find who dropped a Glue table or changed a bucket policy" → CloudTrail. "CloudWatch shows what the code did; CloudTrail shows who called the API."

7Extracting Logs for Audits (skill 3.3.1)

  • Plan before you need it: turn on the right logs (CloudTrail trails with data events for sensitive buckets, S3 server access logs, VPC flow logs, Glue and Lambda logs, database audit logs for Redshift and RDS) and set retention to match policy
  • Centralize: deliver logs to one S3 bucket (often in a separate log-archive account) with encryption, restricted access and lifecycle rules
  • Extract: CloudWatch Logs export to S3, subscription filters to Firehose → S3, CloudTrail trail to S3, Athena queries that write results for the auditor, Logs Insights query exports
  • Preserve evidence: S3 Object Lock, versioning, CloudTrail log file validation, restricted delete
  • Give auditors read-only access to the logs, not to the systems

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Kestrel Freight wants the on-call team notified whenever an AWS Glue job fails. What is the simplest automated solution?

  • AAn EventBridge rule on the Glue job state change that sends to an SNS topic
  • BManually check the Glue console each morning for failed runs and tell the team
  • CAn S3 lifecycle rule on the bucket that holds the job logs
  • DA larger Glue worker type with automatic retries enabled
Show the answer

Answer: A. Glue publishes job state-change events to EventBridge, and a rule can send failures to SNS to notify the team.

S2Which TWO tools are best for querying years of application and CloudTrail logs stored in S3 and for near-real-time log search and dashboards respectively? (Select TWO.)

  • AAmazon Glacier Select
  • BAmazon OpenSearch Service fed by Firehose for search and dashboards
  • CAmazon Macie
  • DAmazon Athena for SQL queries on the logs in S3
  • EAWS Direct Connect
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Athena queries logs in S3 cheaply with SQL, and OpenSearch provides real-time search and dashboards.

S3An engineer needs to know who deleted an AWS Glue table last week. Which service provides this?

  • AAWS CloudTrail
  • BAmazon CloudWatch metrics
  • CAWS Glue job bookmarks
  • DAmazon Athena workgroups
Show the answer

Answer: A. CloudTrail records API calls with the caller identity, the action and the time.

S4An EMR cluster is terminated at the end of each job, and the team still needs the step and container logs for troubleshooting. What should they do?

  • AKeep the cluster running forever so that the logs stay on its nodes
  • BDisable logging on the cluster to avoid storage charges
  • CConfigure the cluster's log URI so that logs are archived to S3
  • DCopy the logs by hand from each node before the termination
Show the answer

Answer: C. EMR archives logs to the S3 location in the log URI, so they remain after the cluster terminates.

S5An auditor needs evidence of access to a sensitive S3 bucket for the past two years. Which TWO preparations support this? (Select TWO.)

  • ATurn off S3 server access logs
  • BDelete logs after 30 days
  • CTurn on CloudTrail data events for the bucket with a trail delivering to S3
  • DRetain the logs in an encrypted, access-restricted S3 bucket with lifecycle rules for the required period
  • ERely only on the 90-day CloudTrail event history
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Data events record object-level access, and a trail with retained logs provides long-term evidence. Event history is limited to 90 days of management events.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Three signals Metrics (CloudWatch) = health; logs (CloudWatch Logs) = what happened; CloudTrail = who did what
Alarms OK / ALARM / INSUFFICIENT_DATA; thresholds and periods; composite, anomaly detection; actions: SNS, Lambda, Auto Scaling
Events EventBridge on Glue/EMR/crawler state changes → SNS/Lambda
Pipeline alarms Job failed or slow, iterator age, Lambda errors/throttles, DLQ depth, data freshness, zero rows
CloudWatch Logs Log groups/streams, retention (default never expire), metric filters, subscription filters (Kinesis, Firehose, Lambda), export to S3, Logs Insights (fields filter stats sort)
Log analysis Insights (quick), Athena (SQL on S3, partition), OpenSearch (search, dashboards), EMR/Spark (huge volumes)
Glue/EMR troubleshooting Glue: metrics, continuous logging, Spark UI, job run insights; EMR: log URI to S3, YARN/Spark History, managed scaling
CloudTrail Management events (history 90 days), data events (off by default), Insights; trail → S3; log file validation
Audit extraction Enable early, central log bucket, encryption, Object Lock/versioning, read-only auditor access
